scope: Experiment F cross-fitted threshold transport diagnostic only; no method optimization.

dataset.control_trajectory_resolution: approximately one trajectory, or 3–4%, in each outer-training set

research_question: Is held-out false-intervention failure primarily caused by optimistic in-sample threshold calibration, or does it persist with out-of-training-sample control scores?

collusion_role_assignment.pattern: roles = {a: ("colluder" if a in colluder_pair else "honest")

observer_prompt_style_audit.interpretation: Paired identities and roles match, but separate upstream honest/control style arrays mean that their honest system-prompt style is not always condition-matched.

caveats: Observer identities and honest roles are paired, but 32 of 62 observer identity pairs use different honest prompt styles across conditions.

domain_shift_audit.quantile_reporting_rule: reported only when domain has at least 10 controls

methodology.risk_aggregation: mean of the two honest-observer decision scores

normalization.name: empirical strict-left tail rank
normalization.formula: count(training-control trajectory maxima < raw prefix risk) / n

threshold_selection.quantile_method: higher plus nextafter for inclusive >= rule

methodology.runtime_policy: first normalized prefix risk >= threshold; stop; no round 4

limitations: Only 31 matched scenario pairs and 1–3 held-out controls per domain.
Empirical tail-rank normalization has no formal conformal or distribution-free guarantee.
The model-specific normalization reference is scored in-sample; cross-fitting applies to calibration observations.
Round 4 is only a proxy boundary and no real-world intervention cost was measured.
Layer 28 and the sentinel architecture were fixed before Experiment F.
